procedure.name: Manoeuvre detection and characterisation
procedure.purpose: Detect that an object has departed from its orbital state, establish whether the departure is real, characterise the burn by direction and magnitude, and assess whether the resulting geometry changes the threat picture. This is the most frequently executed analytical procedure and the foundation of nearly every other one.
entry_conditions: Residual plot shows a sustained departure from the zero line
A provider reports a possible or verified manoeuvre
An object of interest fails to appear where its state predicts
A predictive surveillance check shows drift rate or longitude inconsistent with the last known state
not_this_procedure_when: The headcount is greater than one, in which case enter separation, breakup or UCT discovery first and treat manoeuvre as a supporting assessment
The departure is explained by epoch age or an observation gap, in which case there is no manoeuvre to characterise
The object is in a launch or orbit-injection sequence, where planned burns are processed under launch

steps.action: Verify the state before believing the departure. Check the epoch age of the element set the residuals are computed against, and the observation density either side of the departure.
steps.why: A departure from a starved or stale fit is propagation error, not a burn. Skipping this step is the single most common way a manoeuvre report becomes an artefact report.
steps.common_error: Calling a manoeuvre off a single outlying observation rather than a sustained departure.

steps.action: Determine from the residuals whether the departure is in-plane or out-of-plane.
steps.why: This single read narrows the burn direction before any numbers arrive. In-plane points to in-track or radial; out-of-plane points to cross-track, and therefore to inclination or RAAN, which is the expensive and deliberate kind.

steps.action: Request a post-manoeuvre DC table in the standard format, with the standard verbiage block.
steps.why: Consistency of format is what lets a crew read a manoeuvre the same way every time under time pressure. The verbiage block is copy-ready for the report.

steps.action: Characterise the burn from the Delta column. In-track produces a change in period, eccentricity and possibly argument of perigee. Radial produces a change in eccentricity and argument of perigee only. Cross-track produces a change in inclination or RAAN.
steps.why: The element signature identifies the burn direction without needing the provider to state it, which means the operator can challenge a provider assessment rather than accept it.

steps.action: Sanity-check the magnitude against the regime. Establish whether the stated delta-v and the resulting altitude and drift changes are consistent with each other.
steps.why: Approximate physical relationships are a filter against solver artefacts. A delta-v that cannot produce the stated altitude change means one of the two numbers is wrong.

steps.action: Compare against the object's own pattern of life. Establish whether timing, magnitude and direction are consistent with routine station-keeping.
steps.why: Intent is read against a baseline, not in isolation. A burn consistent with pattern of life is usually housekeeping. A break in an established pattern is itself a signal and can matter more than the burn.

steps.action: Assess the resulting geometry. Request a neighbourhood constrained by inclination and RAAN, and establish whether the new state closes on, opens from, or plane matches any object of interest.
steps.why: A manoeuvre matters because of where it leads, not because it happened. The geometry after the burn is the reportable content.

steps.action: Report, stating clearly whether the manoeuvre is possible or verified, with a confidence level and the supporting phenomenology.
steps.why: The distinction between possible and verified drives what the recipient does next. Collapsing the two is a reporting failure even when the assessment is right.

decision_points.question: Is the departure explained by data quality rather than by the object moving?

branches.condition: Epoch age exceeds the working limit, or observation density collapsed before the departure
branches.then: Treat as unassessable. Request updated states and observations covering the period. Do not report a manoeuvre.

branches.condition: State is current and observations are dense either side

decision_points.question: Is this consistent with the object's established pattern of life?

branches.condition: Consistent in timing, magnitude and direction
branches.then: Assess as routine. Report if the object is of standing interest, stating the pattern of life assessment.

branches.condition: Inconsistent, or the established pattern has ceased
branches.then: Assess as a manoeuvre of interest. Escalate the assessment of resulting geometry.

decision_points.question: Does the resulting geometry establish or close on a proximity relationship?

branches.condition: The new state closes on, plane matches, or parks relative to another object
branches.then: Transition to the RPO procedure while continuing manoeuvre reporting.
Report the manoeuvre and continue custody.

reporting.condition: Report where the object is of standing interest, where the manoeuvre establishes or changes a proximity relationship, or where an established pattern of life has broken.
must_state: Whether the manoeuvre is possible or verified, with confidence
Resulting geometry and any affected objects
Supporting phenomenology and any limitations such as collection gaps
reporting.escalation: Verbal where the resulting geometry places an object of interest in proximity to a protected asset.

closure_criteria: A new post-manoeuvre state is established and observations return to the zero line
The resulting geometry is assessed and reported
Custody is stable across at least the tasking interval
Any transition to a follow-on procedure is opened and linked
